description: Laboratory experiments are based upon the corresponding theory course EEPC-301 and EEPC-311. An updated list of experiments is floated by the course coordinator before the beginning of each semester.
outcomes: Apply economic dispatch and load frequency control for multi-area power systems.
Understand different protection schemes and plot their operating characteristics.
Understand the impact of reactive power compensation on transmission line performance.
Analyze the operation of solar and wind energy systems.
experiments: Perform load frequency control using SIMULINK considering different controllers.
Perform an economic load dispatch study using GAMS software.
Study and plot the operating characteristics of an overcurrent relay.
Study and plot the operating characteristics of a differential relay.
Study and plot the operating characteristics of overvoltage and undervoltage relays.
Study and plot the operating characteristics of under-frequency and over-frequency relays.
Study and plot the operating characteristics of a Buchholz relay.
Study and plot the operating characteristics of a microprocessor based overcurrent relay.
Study and plot the operating characteristics of a negative sequence relay.
Study and plot the operating characteristics of a reverse power relay.
Study the behaviour of a transmission line using reactive power compensators.
Study a solar PV simulator using a PV emulator and a wind power simulator using a wind emulator.
Complete a hardware-based design project based on the above experiments.
